title: Hybrid streaming scheduler: memory-sensitivity tuning for mixed-length prompts
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Reduce P99 latency spikes and OOM pressure for mixed prompt/response workloads by tuning the continuous (streaming) batching scheduler to be memory-sensitive across variable-length dialogs. We will not replace the runtime but introduce adaptive admission and soft-preemption heuristics that coordinate with KV cache slab management and GPU slab compaction signals. The work includes a small runtime change (scheduler admission policy), a KV eviction/TTL tuning, and observability additions to measure per-slot residency and fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P99 end-to-end latency for mixed-length production trace reduced by >= 15% compared to baseline phase A under identical QPS. 2) Incidence of cudaOutOfMemory/non-recoverable OOMs reduced to 0 in stress replay for 72-hour run. 3) Unit-cost (tokens/sec per GPU) change within +/-5% or justified by latency gains. 4) New metrics and dashboards show KV residency and slab fragmentation per GPU node.
experiment_plan: A/B rollout on Dedicated pool: stage-1 (canary) 5% traffic, stage-2 25%, stage-3 100% if targets met. Variants: (V0) baseline, (V1) admission-window + length-elastic buckets, (V2) V1 + soft-preempt KV slab pin/evict hint, (V3) V2 + reduced prefix-caching TTL for >1024-token contexts. Each variant runs 48-hour production replay and synthetic spike test. We will run per-variant meminfo and KV heatmap collection and compare.
metrics:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms)
- tokens/sec per GPU
- KV cache hit rate (by prefix-length bins)
- KV slab fragmentation (%)
- cudaMemoryReserved vs cudaMemoryAllocated trends
- OOM counts and graceful-fallback invocations
- Scheduler admission/rejection rate by length bucket
risks:
- Over-aggressive eviction could regress effective latency for long-running dialogs.
- Tight memory alarms might increase cold-priming calls and slightly raise token cost.
- Scheduler complexity increases risk of unforeseen contention between batching and KV operations.
- Rolling back may require a fast fallback to baseline admission policy and immediate KV reclaiming; must be automated.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + long-run integration in staging with production trace replay. 2) Canary on a single Dedicated shard (5%) for 24-48h. 3) Observe metrics and run stress bursts (50% QPS for 15m) before expanding to 25%. 4) If metrics stable, expand to remaining Dedicated capacity. 5) For Hosted customers, do a conservative config push (V1 only) with opt-in flag for now.

2026-03-06 - Performance lab: Small benchmark (gpt-13B-ish model) shows V1 reduces slot co-location on GPU by 12% and KV slab fragmentation metric by 18% in synthetic mixed workload.
2026-03-08 - Security review: No secret/data-path change; KV hints are control-plane only. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-10 - Ops: Added Grafana panels for per-node slab fragmentation, KV-residency by length-bucket, and admission-rejection rate. Canary job configured to emit additional traces to /debug/slot-residency.

2026-03-11 - Thomas Nguyen: Canary (5%) started at 02:00 UTC. Early telemetry: p99 down ~9% initially, KV hit-rate stable, but tokens/sec dropped 3.2% on one noisy shard — investigating preemption budget threshold.
